title: New to game dev and never used ai for it
author: Special_Quit_2378
selftext:
Hi,

  
Can someone help me figure out how to get started building games with ai?

I have heard godot is good but genuinely when I went to set it up did not really understand it.

  
I figure one of these models can help me do it, what is the setup I should use to get started?

And then as someone who has experience in game dev, what is your current setup?

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
Ai is smart enough to work with most engines these days and godot is documented well enough so.

Have you done any ai projects so far? Comics, videos or writing?

It is pretty much the same process unless you want it to be completely automated; "vibe coding" is basically what you want if you want AI to do almost everything

replies.author: Special_Quit_2378
replies.body: I have done some ai projects! I mean I have used ai for coding but just not game dev

replies.author: Square-Yam-3772
replies.body: then you already know how it works. game dev is really just another coding project for AIs

comments.author: erofamiliar
comments.body:
So, I'm a hobbyist. My recommendation is that you find a good tutorial and run through that \*first\*. It's going to be a nightmare if the AI gives you a list of things to do to get a specific result, and you have to keep asking "Where's that. Where's that button. How do I get that. Where is that. WHAT is that. Signals? Nodes? 2D view? 3D view? Resources????", or if it makes assumptions about how your game is structured and you don't know enough to correct it.

[https://youtu.be/LOhfqjmasi0](https://youtu.be/LOhfqjmasi0)

This is one by brackeys that I think is pretty good. Using an AI to code is fine, but having some familiarity with the engine is going to save you a ton of time and hardship. Once you think you get it, something like Sonnet 4.5 or Gemini 3 is great at helping with code, but Sonnet likes to make assumptions about how your scene is set up. 

Don't think of AI as a "do everything" tool. Think of AI as a really smart guy on the phone with you. A lot of the challenge comes from adequately explaining what you want and how you have things set up.

replies.author: Special_Quit_2378
replies.body: Hm ok, thank you for the link! Okay yeah seems like I need to familiarize myself with an engine first, which engine do you use? I'm probably going to be a hobbyist if I get into it

replies.author: erofamiliar
replies.body: I use Godot! It seems like UE5 and Unity are more powerful, but compile times make my poor ADHD-riddled brain upset and I really enjoy how easy Godot is to learn and use comparatively.

comments.author: gastro_psychic
comments.body: I would suggest starting with Love2D and Codex CLI. It's easy to create a rudimentary 2d first person shooter (or any other type of game) with one prompt. And from there you can build upon it.

replies.author: Special_Quit_2378
replies.body: I love codex. Codex is so good. It's so smart compared to everything else. Is Love2D the engine you use?

replies.author: gastro_psychic
replies.body:
I have played around with Love2D. I like that you can build a game in pure code without an editor. I'm stepping into game development a little bit. Not an expert at all.

Codex works so well on its own. I haven't found a need for MCP's, etc, etc. It works so well for planning and implementation.

comments.author: Joemac_
comments.body: AI might do the heavy lifting but it’s not going to grant you fundamentals. You’ll have to learn how to program and use godot before you can reasonably make a game

replies.author: Special_Quit_2378
replies.body:
This seems to be the answer I was looking for, also seems to be the consensus! Learn the craft and then use AI to enhance it. What is your current set up?

Also this is going to sounds stupid but I have used Unity a sum total of 1 time. Where in a stack of something like using Unreal engine or making fortnite games using verse does ai coding sit?

replies.author: Joemac_
replies.body:
I just make the game as normal and use AI to help when I forget syntax or point me to methods, properties, libraries, etc I'm unaware of when needed. On occasion I might use it to make placeholder sprites.

Thats what I would call my "current setup". I don't know anything about fortnite.

comments.author: Aadi_880
comments.body: You should probably find a tutorial first BEFORE you try to use AI on it. AI can do a lot of the heavy lifting but you will get stumped when something eventually bugs.

replies.author: Aadi_880
replies.body: Brackeys on youtube have tutorials on Unity and Godot. His tutorials are always easy to follow so I recommend it to at least learn the ropes and know where every button is and how they interact.

replies.author: Gone2MyMetalhead
replies.body:
I second Brackeys and starting there. AI can be very helpful but it can also massively over complicate things, especially if you don’t have some understanding of the engine. Also great for providing customized tutorials once you know the questions to ask. 

Also, I’ve yet to see AI give much help in game design fundamentals. If you’re new to the space watching a few tutorials on gameplay, etc (independent of engine) is useful.

comments.author: tilthevoidstaresback
comments.body:
Here's my workflow:

1. Gemini Pro plan.
2. Set up a Gem to help you Synthesize the next step.
3. Use NotebookLM to gather as many resources about the coding language you're using. Synthesize documents in varying categories. Set aside.
4. Repeat step 3 but for the engine you want to use.
5. Repeat step 4 but with AI assisted coding.
6. Create a Gem with all of those documents compiled and uploaded, and give it a profile that is ready to be your assistant.
7. Use the Gem to write the code, or check your code, or bug fix, or teach you how to code in the first place. 


One really useful use for this is when you're following a youtube  tutorial and then they tell you to click something that doesn't exist in your version, halting the progress. Open up your gem, provide it the URL and the timestamp, explain your problem and ask it how to continue. 


I'm sorry for rushing the language, I'm busy at the moment, but just copy this workflow into Gemini and ask it what I'm talking about and it'll break it down.

replies.author: Special_Quit_2378
replies.body: What is a gem? Is a gem an instance of Gemini? Sorry, I'm unfamiliar with this.

comments.author: mysticfallband
comments.body:
While AI can be great for gamedev, you have to understand how the game engine works to fully utilise it.

AI mostly works as a multiplier of your skills. So if you don't know much about gamedev, it's likely that it won't do much for you.

Use AI to learn required skills, if you prefer. Then see where you can introduce AI tools or mechanics to improve your game.
